newsitem.title: USA: Universal to increase film offerings - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Universal to increase film offerings - WSJ.

text.p: Seagram Co Ltd's Universal Studios plans to double the number of films it produces by 2000, the Wall Street Journal said.
In its electronic edition on Tuesday, the Journal said the decision reflects Universal Pictures' Chairman Casey Silver's effort to limit the company's risk in a volatile film business.
"We think that more trips to the plate and a broader diversity of product creates a critical mass moving forward, which we think is strategically beneficial," Silver said.
The move comes at a time when other movie studios are scaling back the number of films they release each year.
This year, Universal -- which is 80 percent owned by Seagram -- plans just 12 releases. In contrast, Walt Disney Co plans 25 releases.

In addition, the Journal said Universal is looking for new financing partners to pay for the change. Unnamed sources were quoted by the Journal as saying it is close to finalizing $1 billion in film financing with Citicorp's Citibank.
